html:
The Grito de Lares was a rising for Puerto Rican independence from Spain on 23 September 1868. Several hundred rebels took the mountain town of Lares and declared the Republic of Puerto Rico.

It was organised from exile by Ramon Emeterio Betances and other nationalists. Spanish troops crushed it the next day at the town of San Sebastian. The rebels were jailed but later freed in an amnesty.

Though short, the Grito became the founding event of Puerto Rican nationalism, and its flag is still flown by independence supporters. It came only weeks before the Ten Years' War began in Cuba. Spain soon granted reforms, including the end of slavery in 1873, and in the 20th century nationalists took up its cause.
sum: The Grito de Lares was a rising for Puerto Rican independence from Spain on 23 September 1868. Several hundred rebels took the mountain town of Lares and declared the Republic of Puerto Rico.
